patients.summary: Healthy elementary school teacher who joined the practice at 27 with one prior term delivery and a history of gallstones. Her second pregnancy brought threatened preterm labor at 32 weeks and GBS colonization before an uncomplicated term delivery in 2025; her third ended at 28 weeks in July 2026 with ruptured membranes and preterm labor in an anencephalic pregnancy and a stillbirth.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller is a 27 y/o teacher whose primary care doctor left her old office over the summer. Heard about the membership practice from a coworker. Explained the membership and that her insurance still covers labs, imaging and prescriptions. She signed up online during the call. New patient visit booked 9/12 at 3:45 pm (after school). Sent the records release form so we can get her old chart. Asked her to bring a list of any medicines and her vaccine card.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
27 y/o woman establishing care. Previous PCP left practice this summer; records release signed, request out.

She feels well and has no complaints today. Teaches second grade, school year just started.

PMH: Gallstones seen on an abdominal ultrasound in spring 2022 at her old office, done after a single bout of upper belly pain that went away by itself. Never saw a surgeon. No pain, nausea or food intolerance since. Otherwise healthy.
PSH: none.
OB/GYN: G1P1. One term vaginal delivery in 2021, no complications in pregnancy or labor. Periods regular. Last Pap 2021 per patient, normal, done at her old office.
Meds: none. Not on contraception; she and her husband are open to another child down the road but not trying.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: Mother had one miscarriage. A second cousin on her mother's side was born with spina bifida. No early heart disease, diabetes or cancer that she knows of.
SH: Married, lives in Springfield with her husband and their child. Never smoked, no vaping. Alcohol a drink or two a month. No drug use. Walks most evenings.

ROS: negative except as above.

Exam: Vitals as recorded. BMI about 24. Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no RUQ tenderness, Murphy negative, no masses. No edema. Skin without rashes. Mood and affect normal.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
1. Establishing care, health maintenance. CBC, CMP, fasting lipids, one-time HIV and hep C screening today. Pap due 2024; will do at her physical next spring. Flu and updated COVID shots offered; she'd rather come back in October once the new COVID vaccine is in.
2. History of gallstones, asymptomatic. No workup needed. Reviewed what biliary pain feels like and when to call.
3. Future pregnancy: start a prenatal vitamin with folic acid a few months before trying. She'll let us know.

Return for annual physical in spring, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Willa, everything from Tuesday's blood work is back and looks good. Blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol are all in the healthy range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do. See you in October for shots.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Records received by fax from previous PCP office, 41 pages, scanned to chart.

Abstracted:
- Cervical cytology 06/2021: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
- Abdominal ultrasound 03/2022: cholelithiasis, otherwise unremarkable; no gallbladder wall thickening.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete per state registry printout; Tdap 2021 during pregnancy; COVID primary series 2021.
- No chronic medications on last med list.

Routed to PCP for review.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Here after school for vaccines. Feels well, no fever. Not pregnant. No prior vaccine reactions.
Flu vaccine 0.5 mL IM right deltoid. COVID updated vaccine 0.3 mL IM left deltoid. VIS for both given.
Waited 15 min in the lobby without issue. Registry updated.

medications.drug_text: folic acid 0.8 MG / prenatal multivitamin Oral Tablet

documents.title: Starting a vitamin
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! My husband and I have decided to start trying for a second baby sometime this summer. You mentioned the prenatal vitamin last fall. Is there one you'd recommend, or can you send one in so insurance covers it? Thanks!

documents.title: RE: Starting a vitamin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's great news. I sent a prescription prenatal vitamin with 800 mcg of folic acid to your pharmacy, one a day. Starting now is perfect timing. We'll go over anything else at your physical next month, and once you have a positive test let us know and we'll get you set up with obstetrics.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based preparation. Specimen adequacy: satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.
reports.conclusion: Negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam. Feels well. Started the prenatal vitamin last month, tolerating it; mild nausea the first week only. Plans to start trying in July after school is out. Cycles regular, LMP 4/2.
No gallbladder symptoms.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily. NKDA.
SH unchanged: never smoker, rare alcohol, plans to stop once trying.

Exam: Vitals as charted, weight up slightly from fall. Well. Thyroid normal. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts without masses, no nipple discharge, no axillary nodes. Abdomen soft, nontender. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, vaginal mucosa normal, cervix without lesions; Pap collected. Bimanual: uterus normal size, no adnexal masses or tenderness. Extremities no edema.

PHQ-2 0.

A/P:
1. Preventive care. Pap today (last 2021). CBC, BMP, TSH before pregnancy. Up to date on Tdap (2021) and COVID. Flu in the fall.
2. Preconception. Continue prenatal vitamin. Avoid alcohol once trying. Reviewed the cousin's spina bifida: folic acid at this dose is the standard recommendation and she is taking it. Will refer to OB when pregnant.
3. Hx gallstones: quiet.

RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Pap and labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Willa, your Pap came back normal and your blood count, chemistries and thyroid are all normal. Next Pap in three years. Good luck this summer!

documents.title: Positive test
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Good morning, I took a home test this morning and it's positive! My last period started September 22. What do I do next? Also I still haven't had my flu shot, is it ok to get it while pregnant?

documents.title: RE: Positive test
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Congratulations! Yes, the flu shot is recommended in pregnancy. I booked you a nurse visit Thursday at 3:30 to confirm the test, give the flu shot and send the obstetrics referral. Keep taking your prenatal vitamin.

documents.title: Pregnancy test and flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Urine hCG in office: positive. LMP 9/22/24, about 4 1/2 weeks. Mild fatigue, no bleeding or cramping. Taking prenatal vitamin daily.
Flu vaccine (trivalent, preservative-free) 0.5 mL IM left deltoid, VIS given, tolerated.
OB referral sent to the hospital obstetrics group per PCP; she will get a call for an intake visit around 8 weeks. Reviewed bleeding/severe pain precautions.

documents.title: Referral follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: OB office confirmed referral received. Intake visit scheduled 11/18. Patient aware.
